en: The Sampaguita, the national flower, is a white jasmine that blooms year-round and is widely observed in Filipino gardens and offered during civic events.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into steep mountain slopes, creating observable, stepped agricultural landscapes that follow the natural contours of the Cordillera mountains.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their houses with observable natural harvests like colorful kiping, which are leaf-shaped rice paste decorations dyed with natural food coloring.
National Scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying mango trees with observable potassium nitrate solution induces year-round flowering, transforming the local fruit environment and agriculture.
The original Philippine flag was first unfurled from the observable balcony of the Aguinaldo Shrine in Kawit, Cavite, during the declaration of independence on June 12, 1898.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is observable in the dense dipterocarp forests of Mindanao, where it relies on tall trees like the dipterocarp for nesting.
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources, an executive branch agency, enforces laws protecting observable natural resources like the Tubbataha Reef from illegal fishing.
Many Philippine languages use specific observable terms for local plants, like the Tagalog word narra for the national tree, which yields distinct red hardwood.
Ilocano weavers create the observable geometric patterns of Abel Iloco textiles using traditional wooden looms and locally grown cotton threads dyed with natural plant extracts.
During his exile in Dapitan, hero Jose Rizal built an observable waterworks system using local stones and clay pipes to bring spring water to the community.
Under the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, every Filipino citizen has the observable civic duty to segregate biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste at the household level.
The traditional value of bayanihan is historically observed when neighbors physically carry a lightweight, natural nipa hut on bamboo poles to relocate it for a family.
